reports.title: Rafe Angelo
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths
Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The risk assessment of Ms Angelo followed NICE guidelines at the time but | remain concerned that no simple weight check is done to check maternal BMI and that GROW charts only pick up 50-55% of cases where growth restriction occurs
CTG is not currently available in birthing centres and should be considered in emergency situations such as this case especially if it is not possible to transport the mother to hospital
The SIRI investigation highlighted that the instruction given to the maternity support worker was not clear about what category of transfer was required
Consider where the "Use of Standby Points" policy needs to be refreshed to make it clearer and more consistent
Poor technical quality of the CTG readings at a crucial time especially given "this was the first trace in am emergency situation
Recording all requests to transfer to hospital in notes and active | consideration by midwives

reports.title: Louie Johnston: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: CTG trace monitoring equipment that was in use in the labour ward required staff to switch from a CTG trace screen to a K2 electronic recording screen during delivery. This meant that a graphic representation of the CTG trace was not clearly visible at all times. Instead , midwifery staff were required to crouch down and record numeric data from the CTG displayed on a small LED screen. The Trust identified this as counter-productive and raised the issue with the manufacturer of the system. To date

A review of staff training records indicated that an obstetric registrar involved in the delivery was not up to date with mandated annual CTG training. Additionally, the obstetric consultant had not completed annual training which required the session to be repeated following the death of Louie Johnston. Systems in place at the Trust did not ensure that all medical staff had completed requisite training .

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with the clarity and reliability of cardiotocography (CTG) monitoring during labour. The earlier report cites poor technical quality of CTG readings at a critical moment, while the later report describes equipment that forces staff to switch screens, obscuring the graphic trace.
